rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.e1: Counterattack: let us think from White's side, with White to move. Game Mr-witty × fakroune, Lichess 2020. Start with the question from the previous lesson: what does Black threaten?
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.e2: They threaten mate: the queen on f2 captures the pawn on g2, defended by the knight on f4. Defending g2 looks natural. First, look at the black king and at your checks.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.p: Find the strongest move for White.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.certo: The queen captures the pawn on e5 with check, along the diagonal that leads to the king on h8.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the queen to e5: it captures the pawn with check, along the diagonal to the king on h8.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.e6d5.1: The bishop goes to d5 and defends g2.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.e6d5.2: The queen gives check on h4. After the king goes to g1, the knight gives mate on e2. Defending was not enough.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.e6d5.3: Back to the position: before defending g2, look for a check that arrives first.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.d6e7.1: The queen goes to e7, but it neither gives check nor defends g2.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.d6e7.2: The black queen captures the pawn on g2 with mate.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.err.d6e7.3: Back to the position: before defending g2, look for a check that arrives first.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not arrive before the threat on g2. Look for a check.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: Black threatens mate, and whoever checks first can arrive first.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.l1: The black king has no square: g8 belongs to the bishop on e6, and g7 to the queen. Only the rook on f8 can block the check.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.l2: The rook goes to f6 and blocks the check.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.l3: The queen captures the rook with mate. White gave mate before the black queen could reach g2.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex1.l4: This is a counterattack: instead of defending, you answer with a stronger threat that arrives first. In positions like this, when your opponent threatens mate, look at your checks before defending.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.e1: Counterattack: now with Black, in the Game Blackmen60 × MACHINOVISH, Lichess 2021. The rook on d7 attacks your queen on c7.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.e2: And White threatens mate: the rook goes to d8 and uncovers the check of the bishop on b5, a double check. Saving the queen and stopping the mate is hard. First, look at the white king on d1.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.p: Find the strongest move for Black.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.certo: Your queen captures the pawn on c2 with check. It is defended by the bishop on b3, and the king cannot capture it.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the queen to c2: it captures the pawn with check, defended by the bishop on b3.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.b3c2.1: The bishop captures the pawn on c2 with check, but your queen is still attacked by the rook.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.b3c2.2: The king gets out of check on e2. Your queen is still attacked, and the mate on d8 remains: you cannot hold both, and White wins.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.b3c2.3: Back to the position: the attacked queen can give check. Look for the check that leads to mate.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.c7d7.1: The queen captures the rook on d7 with check, but the rook was defended by the queen on h3 and the bishop on b5.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.c7d7.2: The queen on h3 recaptures with check. Black lost the queen for a rook.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.c7d7.3: Back to the position: the attacked queen can give check. Look for the check that leads to mate.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.e8g8.1: You castle and take the king away from the mate on d8, but the queen on c7 is still attacked.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.e8g8.2: The rook captures your queen. White wins.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.err.e8g8.3: Back to the position: the attacked queen can give check. Look for the check that leads to mate.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not solve it: your queen is still attacked, and the mate on d8 remains. Look for a check.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: start with your queen's checks.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.l1: The white king has only one square, e1: d2 belongs to the bishop on e3, and e2 to your queen.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.l3: The queen goes to f2, defended by the bishop on e3, and gives mate. The mate on d8 never happened.
rot.counterattack.ideia.ex2.l4: Another counterattack. In positions like this, the attacked piece can be the one that attacks: a check that forces the reply comes before saving it.
rot.counterattack.demos.reiExposto.1: Counterattack: Black again, in the Game Faruku × uykucugergedan, Lichess 2021. Your king is on e3, among the white pieces, and they threaten mate: the queen goes to c1 with check.
rot.counterattack.demos.reiExposto.2: Capturing the rook on d1 with the bishop looks natural. But after the capture, the white queen gives mate on c3. The white king on f1 is exposed too: let us look for a check.
rot.counterattack.demos.reiExposto.3: The bishop goes to e2 with check. The white king only has the e1 square: f2 belongs to your king, and g1 and g2 to the rook on g8.
rot.counterattack.demos.reiExposto.5: The rook goes to g1 and gives mate: your king on e3 covers d2 and f2 and defends the bishop on e2.
rot.counterattack.demos.reiExposto.6: In positions like this, both kings are exposed. Whoever gives the check that forces the reply reaches mate first.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.1: Counterattack: now with White, in the Game husowe × jcpino, Lichess 2022. Black threatens mate: the queen on a6 captures the bishop on a1.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.2: Running with the king to c1 is not enough: the queen captures the bishop on a1 with mate anyway. Look at the black king: your queen and the knight on g7 are already close to it.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.3: The queen captures the pawn on h7 with check. You give up the queen: the black king is forced to capture it.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.4: The king captures the queen on h7.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.5: The rook goes to h3 and gives mate. The king has no square: g8 is occupied by the black rook, and the knight on g7 is defended by the pawn on f6.
rot.counterattack.demos.entrega.6: In positions like this, the counterattack can cost a piece, even the queen. What counts is reaching mate before your opponent.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.1: Counterattack: now with Black, in the Game TSMFTW × FIDE_SPARSH, Lichess 2023. The white queen on f7 attacks your rook on f8.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.2: You have checks on g3 and on f4. But the knight on e2 captures the queen on g3, and the white queen captures the knight on f4: after each check, the rook on f8 stays attacked.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.p: Find the strongest move for Black.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.certo: The rook on f8 captures the queen on f7.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.revela: The move is the rook to f7: it captures the white queen.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.err.d6g3: The queen gives check on g3, but the knight on e2 captures it. If your rook captures the queen on f7, the rook on a7 captures the one on a8 with check.
The knight on e2 captures your queen. White wins.
The check did not stop the threat. Back to the position: look again at the white queen on f7.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.err.h5f4: The knight gives check on f4.
The white queen captures the knight. White is a piece up.
The check did not stop the threat. Back to the position: look again at the white queen on f7.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.err.f8g8: The rook leaves f8 for g8 and escapes the attack, but the white queen stays on the seventh rank.
The rook on a7 captures the pawn on e7 and threatens mate: the queen captures on h7, defended by the rook. White wins.
Running with the rook was slower. Back to the position: look again at the white queen on f7.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.err.a8a7: The rook captures the rook on a7, but leaves your rook on f8 undefended.
The queen captures the rook on f8 with mate.
Capturing the rook was slower than the threat. Back to the position: look at the white queen on f7.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.3: The checks did not stop the threat: the white queen kept attacking the rook on f8. The capture removed the attacking piece.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.4: The rook on a7 captures your rook on a8 with check.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.5: The king gets out of check on g7. Black won the queen for a rook.
rot.counterattack.demos.excecao.6: In positions like this, a counterattack only works if it arrives first. If the check does not stop the threat, and a simple move does, the simple move comes first.
rot.counterattack.pratica.valeAqui.enunc: Black threatens to capture the pawn on g3 with the bishop, with check. You have a check at hand: the queen captures the bishop on e5. First, see what each move wins. Does it work here? Play as White.
rot.counterattack.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The rook captured the black queen, which was undefended. The bishop captured on g3 with check, and the king went to h1, off the file of the rook on g6. White won the queen and stays ahead in material. Before the check, look at the captures too: winning the loose queen was worth more than the threat of the bishop.
rot.counterattack.pratica.valeAqui.err.e: The queen captures the bishop with check, but the black queen captures it, and the rook recaptures: the position is equal. Here the check is not the move: the black queen on f5 was undefended.
With the king on g1 or g2, it stands on the file of the rook on g6: the bishop captures the rook on e1 and uncovers the check, and Black wins material back. Take the king to h1, off the g-file.
With the king on g1 or g2, it stands on the file of the rook on g6: the bishop captures the rook on e1 and uncovers the check, and Black wins material back. Take the king to h1, off the g-file.
rot.counterattack.pratica.mateG2.enuncia: White threatens mate on c7 with the queen. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.counterattack.pratica.mateG2.fim: The queen gave check on e2, defended by the pawn on f3, and then gave mate on g2. You reached mate before White.
rot.counterattack.pratica.mateG2.err.h8h: The rook captures the bishop on h7, but White arrives first: the rook on c1 captures on c7 with check, and mate follows soon after. Look for a check.
rot.counterattack.pratica.mateG2.err.c7c: The pawn leaves c7, and the white queen goes to c7 and gives mate. Before defending, look for a check.
rot.counterattack.pratica.mateG2.err2.f3: The pawn gives check, but the white queen captures it, and the mate is gone. Look for the mate with the queen.
rot.counterattack.pratica.fileiraTras.en: White threatens mate on h7 with the queen. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.counterattack.pratica.fileiraTras.fi: The queen captured the knight on g1 with check, and the king had to capture it. The rook on e8 gave mate on e1, on the back rank.
rot.counterattack.pratica.fileiraTras.er: The rook defends h7, but White captures the bishop on h3 and is a piece up. Before defending, look for a check.
The pawn leaves h7, but the white queen captures on h6 with check and trades the queens, and then the rook captures the bishop on h3. Before defending, look for a check.
That move gives no check, and White arrives first: the queen captures the pawn on h7 with mate.
The bishop gives check, but the king captures it, and the mate on h7 remains. Look for the check that leads to mate.
